study: Whittaker et al. 2020, MyTeachingPartner-Math/Science (MTP-M/S) curricula + teacher supports vs BaU, JREE 13(2):177-212 (IES R305A120631)
eval_evidence: Authored by the University of Virginia research team that designed the MTP-M/S curricula and teacher support system ('we designed the MTP-M/S curricula...'); the developers conducted the impact evaluation.
developer_evidence: The research team delivered the curricula, workshops, and online/within-activity supports they developed; they ran the introductory summer workshop and academic-year PD workshops and provided the web-based teacher support system.
cascade_evidence: The developer/research team provided the PD workshops and online supports directly to the participating pre-K teachers; no train-the-trainer / lead-teacher intermediary described.
counterfactual_evidence: Treatment compared to a Business-as-Usual (BaU) control; BaU teachers continued their usual instruction (and submitted videos for measurement parity) but received no MTP-M/S curricula or supports.
coaching_evidence: Teacher support = an introductory summer workshop plus a series of 2.5-hour PD workshops (five in year 1, three in year 2) and online video/within-activity supports; no recurring one-on-one in-class coaching cycles (videos were used for measurement/coding, not individualized coaching feedback).
student_dose_evidence: MTP-M/S is a teacher-delivered math/science curriculum integrated into regular pre-K instruction; no tutoring, pull-out, or student-facing software dose added.
maturity_evidence: Two consecutive single-year cohorts each measured at the end of their first (and only) implementation year; teachers were new to MTP-M/S in the wave used (the experimental Year-1 cohort is first-year; the Year-2 cohort is a separate, attrition-compromised new sample, not the same teachers gaining experience).
